title: vertical-rail — a rotated identity spine down one edge
idea: A narrow full-height spine down one edge carries the wordmark in rotated type, like the spine of a book on a shelf. The remaining field holds an ordinary copy-and-plate composition, framed by that edge.
why_new: nothing in the catalog uses the vertical axis for type or treats an edge as structure.
built_from: a two-column row with a fixed narrow column and a reviewed writing-mode hook.
risk: rotated text is an accessibility hazard and must stay decorative identity, never the H1; below the stacking breakpoint the spine becomes a normal top strip.
